title: Introduce oversubscription safety valve and gentle tenant nudge for regional bursts
author: Marisa Ortega
description: Motivation: recent regional oversubscription incidents caused cascading slowdowns when a small number of tenants burst simultaneously. Existing load-shedding was too coarse (global token buckets) and caused noisy neighbor effects and hard fails. This PR introduces an "oversubscription safety valve": a local, per-zone admission controller that applies proportional pacing when the pool becomes oversubscribed, plus a companion "tenant nudge" mechanism that gently reduces transient tenant pressure via delayed retry hints and short-lived quota nudges. This is implemented as a defensive hotfix that can be toggled by feature flag and has a safe emergency revert path. Changes include: - A new zone-local admission controller (service/overload/safety_valve.go) that tracks oversubscription using short-window SLO debt and target headroom heuristics. - Tenant nudge controller (service/overload/tenant_nudge.go) which returns structured guidance headers and exponential backoff hint tokens for clients when a tenant is identified as bursty. - Deferred warm-standby orchestration notes (deploy/k8s/overlay/standby.yaml) to allow one-off micro-standby kubelets to be brought up quicker in a region when safety valve opens. - Metrics and dashboards (telemetry/metrics.yaml + docs/ops/incident-playbooks.md) for SLO debt, valve-open-rate, tenant-nudge-rate, and latency tail correlation. - Feature flags (pkg/featureflags/flags.go) and an emergency revert script (tools/revert-safety-valve.sh). Backwards compatibility and safety: default behavior is gated off; when enabled defaults are conservative (3% of pool headroom threshold, 500ms minimum nudge delay). The valve is soft by default: it attempts proportional pacing and graceful prefix-drop before any hard reject. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for valve admission logic and tenant token decay (service/overload/*_test.go) - [x] Integration smoke in benchmark-lab to ensure no steady-state regression - [x] Canary rollout strategy documented in deploy/README.md - [x] Telemetry and dashboards wired - [x] Feature-flag gating with kill-switch script Notes: This description is intentionally contiguous (no section breaks) to match PR ingestion tooling expectations.
